post.summary: Request password recovery with a generic response
post.description: Strict 4 KiB JSON, exact approved HTTPS Origin, identity 3/hour and network 10/hour with a minimum 15-minute denial, lasting through any exhausted quota window. Blocked retries do not renew timers. Unknown, malformed, Google-only and ambiguous SMTP outcomes return the same 202 after accepted limiter processing.

X-Bidora-Code-Challenge.description: Random per-request reference for a six-digit recovery code, also returned for ineligible targets.

429.description: Limited; Retry-After reports the effective remaining wait in seconds (1–3600), including identity and network quota windows

post.summary: Consume a single-use recovery token and reset an existing password credential
post.description: New recovery emails contain six numeric digits and link to /recovery_email/{user_id}?challenge_ref={random_reference}. The reference is not authority without the code. Codes are purpose/reference scoped with a server HMAC, expiry, single use, per-reference failure limits and network limits. Legacy strong-token email fragments remain valid. Credentials are submitted only in this JSON body, never in server URLs. When supplied, user_id must match the token owner. Successful reset advances credential/auth epoch and revokes all sessions without issuing a replacement session.

token.description: Six numeric digits plus challenge_ref, or a legacy strong token.

challenge_ref.description: Required with six digits; random issuance reference.
